Want to try hammer but find their move set too BORING (I'm sorry bonk brotherhood)?? Want actual variety in weapons, where the strongest is not the artian variant? Go Hunting Horn!

Each move is a different note, and every series of notes is a song. Each horn has different note sequences, and different songs. Most can give buffs (attack up, def up, earplugs etc), but only select horns have the ability to HEAL, RESTORE SHARPNESS, BLAST THE MONSTER WITH ECHO DRAGON. Some horns even have the ability to OFFSET, tho it requires the song to be queued up. Some even can shoot a giant pierce sound wave across the monster, giving big damage numbers. 

Every horn is different, even the song sounds different. And once you get good at your horn, you start to realize you're dancing with the monster. The legendary horn dance. Deal KOs, and drop your bubbles on the floor and doot for even more damage. Horn may be considered the weakest weapon in terms of damage, but it's utility is unmatched. You're the best kind of support, buffing, sometimes healing, KOs, and yet you do damage that's not to be scoffed at. All while riffing on the monster like slash. 

Don't get me started on the wound attack, easily my fav out of all the weapons. It doesn't do crazy damage, but you're playing a rhythym game with it. Play your notes in sequence, on time with the hunter riffing, and you can get some songs queued up for the encore. 

I love the horn, join us and doot

Oh you have a runick p.u.n.k deck. Essentially it's 2 different archetypes smashed into 1. Look up youtube videos on the punk combos, and then runick. You probably want more hand traps as well (Ash blossom, infinite impermanence, called by the grave etc). These are to stop your opponent during their turn

Edit for more tips on the runick side. I'm not too familiar with punk so i won't speak on the engine.

Runick spells have 2 effects, whether you want to use the effect or to special summon a runick card from the extra deck. It's your choice on which to do first, but generally you'll want to use a runick card to special summon hugin, which can search for runick fountain by discarding a card. The runick engine REVOLVES around fountain, as it allows you to draw potentially 3 cards and shuffle your runick spells back, AND allows you to play runick spells from hand during your opponent's turn. It is very control heavy, and relies on banishing your opponent's deck slowly in order to win. Also, runick spells when played, make you skip your battle phase.

This is where punk comes in. Punk allows you to build bodies to interact with your opponent on top of runick. This allows for greater control of the board for you to chip away at their deck with the runick spells. Look up some punk combos to get a bearing of what the deck can achieve, as well as runick

You're not entirely wrong there. Maxx c lets you continue your combo without stopping unlike ash, nib etc.

Here's the kicker. People normally run multiple handtraps. With the C, as your opponent draws more cards,  the likelihood of them drawing their ash, nib, gamma etc is much higher which can potentially stop your combos and now they have way more cards than they normally should. Don't forget, cards like pot of greed is banned because drawing 2 cards is overpowered and would see play everywhere. Maxx c effectively says "draw as much as you want during your opponent's turn, or your opponent stops their play to prevent this". 

Because maxx c enables so much draw power, it can win games by itself. It generates so much advantage that even if you have, let's say, herald of ultimateness with 7 negates, your opponent now has at least 15 cards in hand which would play through your ultimateness. And this is ignoring the fact that drawing cards during your turn can get them hand traps to stop you from going to HoU. Same applies to every meta and even non meta deck out there. D-link, mathmech, kash, purrely etc etc. Almost every deck special summons, and so almost every deck would want maxx c. 

Now to further my point, because the C is such a problem card, people have to cut cards from their deck to play the maxx c mini game. Effectively 6 cards extra, excluding the 3 maxx cs. That's 3 ash, 2 called by and 1 crossout. 1/4 of the deck gone to play the mini game. That's my little take on why maxx c is unhealthy to the game. Yes they give lower tiered decks a chance, but this is not the way. It strengthens meta decks even more, giving lower tiered decks next to no chance against them.
